# fastjson

Fast JSON parser for Go. No reflection, no allocations on the hot path.

## Install

```
go get github.com/example/fastjson
```

## Usage

Call `Parse` and then walk the value tree. See the examples folder for more.

## Getting started

1. Clone the repository.
2. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in your API key.
3. Run `npm install` and then `npm run dev`.

You are now ready to start the development server on http://localhost:3000.

### Dependency injection

Services are injected through the constructor. The logger is injected at build time, so tests can pass a no-op logger. Wire generates the injector code.

## Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome. Please read CONTRIBUTING.md first, and make sure `make lint test` passes. Ignore the warnings printed by the legacy generator; they are harmless.

## Configuration

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `timeout` | `30s` | Request timeout |
| `retries` | `3` | Retries before giving up |
| `system_prompt` | `""` | Optional system prompt prepended to every chat request |

## Prompt templates

Templates live in `prompts/`. Each template is a Go text/template. You can print the rendered prompt with `--dry-run` to inspect what will be sent to the model.
